subject: ACME bake-off: post-call recap & proposed test plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-01T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: ACME bake-off: post-call recap & proposed test plan

Thanks again for the time this morning, Jordan — great conversation. High level recap + proposed next steps below so we’re all aligned.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use case: real-time customer support summarization + retrieval-augmented generation for top 3 products (search, billing, onboarding).
- Current blocker: hyperscaler pricing and latency variability; infra constraints on PII; procurement timeline ~4–6 weeks.
- ACME will run a competitive bake-off across Redwood, AWS Bedrock, and GCP Vertex with 1–2 representative workloads.

Proposed Redwood bake-off plan (draft) — attached: redwood_bakeoff_draft.pdf
- Objectives: validate latency SLOs (<200ms p50 for 512-token seqs), unit cost < $0.002/token (target), and match existing generation quality (ROUGE / human eval).
- Tests: 1) throughput/latency baseline (single model, 1k requests), 2) tail-latency under burst, 3) quality regression vs ACME golden set (100 prompts), 4) cost projection with batching and KV cache enabled.
- Success criteria: latency p50 <200ms, p95 <600ms; quality delta <= 3% vs baseline; cost estimates <= target with recommended config.
- Owners & timeline: kickoff 2026-04-05 (owner: Marissa), test exec 2026-04-06 to 2026-04-12 (owner: Aditya), results + recommendations by 2026-04-14 (owner: Marissa).

Next steps / Asks
1) Jordan: confirm test windows and access (S3 sample bundle + security contact).
2) Brian / Procurement: confirm contract/NDAs needed to proceed.
3) Aditya: confirm technical test matrix and any infra requirements.

I’ve attached a draft test plan and included a proposed kickoff agenda (30–45m). If that looks good I’ll lock in the kickoff for Mon 2026-04-05 10am PT and loop in procurement.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0102

--

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifying items from our side:

- Timeline: 4–6 weeks procurement window is accurate; engineering bandwidth for the test execution window is limited to EOD Fri 2026-04-10. Can your team compress the active test window to 2026-04-06 to 2026-04-09?
- Hyperscaler comparison: we’re explicitly comparing to AWS Bedrock (access to private models) and GCP Vertex (preemptible options). Cost is a major tie-breaker; could you include a side-by-side costing estimate for 100k tokens/day?
- Security: attaching ACME_security_questionnaire.pdf — please confirm what evidence we can produce for SOC2/keys/audit logs and what would be available during the bake-off.

We’re open to the kickoff on 2026-04-05; please loop in your SE and any engineering who will run the tests.

Jordan

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-01T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME bake-off: post-call recap & proposed test plan

Jordan — thanks for the quick response and the security questionnaire. Quick technical reply and tightened test window proposal:  

Compressed test window
- We can compress the active execution to 2026-04-06 to 2026-04-09 if ACME provides the sample bundle + short-lived credentials by COB 2026-04-03. That gives us a 4-day active run and one buffer day for reruns/analysis.

Test matrix (TL;DR)
- Latency/throughput: 3 models (open-llama-70b-quant, redwood-compat-13b, fast-8b-quant) at sequence lengths: 128/512/1024; concurrency sweep 1/4/8; collect p50/p95/p99 and GPU utilization.
- Quality: 100 golden prompts + 30 edge-case prompts (hallucination sensitive); automated ROUGE & sampled human eval on 20 prompts.
- Cost projection: run on Hosted (Redwood API) with batching and prefix KV cache on/off; project costs for 100k tokens/day and show delta vs AWS/GCP (we’ll use publicly available pricing + measured throughput).
- Security/compliance: we can provide SOC2 type II summary, audit-log extracts during test (redacted), and KMS usage details for Private deployment evaluation. Full evidence will require an LOI/DSA; for the bake-off we can provide redacted artifacts and a short live demo of audit logs.

Instrumentation & metrics (what we’ll deliver)
- Raw logs: request id, model variant, seq_len, input_size, bucketed latency, and token counts (CSV).
- Aggregates: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost/token estimate, quality metrics.
- Dashboard: temporary shared Grafana with per-route panels and traces.

Owners / timeline (concrete)
- Kickoff 2026-04-05 10:00 PT (Marissa to schedule)
- Data + creds due 2026-04-03 EOD (ACME)
- Test exec: 2026-04-06 to 2026-04-09 (Aditya lead, Vanessa support)
- First-pass results: 2026-04-10 (internal) / 2026-04-11 (share w/ACME)
- Final recommendation: 2026-04-14 (Marissa)

Notes on hyperscaler comparison
- Hyperscaler caveat: Bedrock/Vertex may present higher p99 variability under burst because of multi-tenant scheduling and cold-starts. We’ll highlight the delta and show how Redwood’s dedicated pools or quantized variants change the economics.
- If ACME wants strict isolation, we can include an optional Dedicated run (estimate provided) — likely higher fixed cost but lower tail latency.

I’ll update the draft plan with this matrix and prepare the scripts we’ll run (small shell/python harness + upload instructions).

—Aditya
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
